Momentum roughness length

Source: R/metric-aerodynamics.R
ef_zom.Rd

Computes the surface roughness length for momentum transport \(z_{om}\) [m], which controls the friction velocity and the aerodynamic resistance to heat transport of the METRIC energy balance. ef_zom() is the dispatcher of the family: it checks method (no default), forwards the arguments to one of the method functions (which can also be called directly), builds the diagnostic flags and records the provenance.

  • ef_zom_lai(): linear function of the leaf area index, for short (agricultural) crops.

  • ef_zom_ndvi(): exponential function of NDVI / albedo with user-supplied coefficients (to be fitted to points of known roughness).

  • ef_zom_perrier(): Perrier function of LAI, canopy height and the fraction of LAI above half the canopy height, for trees and tall crops.

  • ef_zom_height(): FAO-56 function of the vegetation height, mainly for the surface around a weather station.

Usage

ef_zom(
  lai = NULL,
  ndvi = NULL,
  albedo = NULL,
  coef_1 = NULL,
  coef_2 = NULL,
  f_lai = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  method
)

ef_zom_lai(lai)

ef_zom_ndvi(ndvi, albedo, coef_1, coef_2)

ef_zom_perrier(lai, f_lai, height)

ef_zom_height(height)

Arguments

lai

Numeric. Leaf area index [m2 m-2]. Must be finite and >= 0. Used by "lai" and "perrier".

ndvi

Numeric. Normalised difference vegetation index [-], in [-1, 1]. Used by "ndvi".

albedo

Numeric. Broadband surface albedo [-], in (0, 1]. Used by "ndvi".

coef_1, coef_2

Numeric. Coefficients \(c_1\) [-] and \(c_2\) [-] of the exponential relation, supplied by the user (no default exists). Must be finite. Used by "ndvi".

f_lai

Numeric. Fraction of the leaf area index located above half the canopy height [-], in [0, 1]. Used by "perrier".

height

Numeric. Canopy (vegetation) height [m]. Must be finite and >= 0. Used by "perrier" and "height".

method

Character. The formulation, with no default (the choice is a scientific decision; decision SH-01 is open). One of "lai", "ndvi", "perrier" or "height". Matched exactly.

Value

The method functions return a numeric vector of momentum roughness length \(z_{om}\) [m] with the common length of the inputs, keeping their dim if they are matrices or arrays. Zero values (e.g. lai = 0 or height = 0) are returned unchanged: no minimum roughness is applied (see Details) and such values are rejected by ef_ustar().

ef_zom() returns a list of class earthflux_roughness_length with elements zom (identical to the method function), method, flags (one record per code that holds somewhere: EF_INPUT_NA, a required input is missing; no EF_H_ code applies to \(z_{om}\) while no minimum roughness or terrain factor is implemented) and provenance (method, method function, verification status, inputs used, flag codes evaluated in flags_evaluated, EarthFlux version).

Details

ef_zom_lai() (method = "lai"): $$z_{om} = 0.018\,\mathrm{LAI}$$

ef_zom_ndvi() (method = "ndvi"): $$z_{om} = \exp(c_1\,\mathrm{NDVI}/\alpha + c_2)$$

ef_zom_perrier() (method = "perrier"): $$z_{om} = \left(1 - e^{-p\,\mathrm{LAI}/2}\right) e^{-p\,\mathrm{LAI}/2}\, h$$ with \(p = 1 / (2 (1 - f))\) if \(f < 0.5\) and \(p = 2 f\) otherwise (both branches give \(p = 1\) at \(f = 0.5\)), where \(f\) is f_lai and \(h\) is height.

ef_zom_height() (method = "height"): $$z_{om} = 0.123\,h$$ (FAO-56, chapter 2, box 4, which also gives the zero-plane displacement \(d = 2 h / 3\)).

Assumptions and limitations: the linear LAI relation is meant for short crops; secondary sources report that it underestimates the roughness of maize and that vines and trees need another function. With 1 km MODIS pixels (mixed covers) the roughness of the mean LAI is not the mean roughness of the covers. The Perrier function needs a canopy height map, which MODIS does not provide.

No minimum roughness (0.005 m in METRIC implementations, decision SH-02) and no mountainous-terrain adjustment (SH-03) are applied: both are unverified and values are never silently modified. The presets of earthflux() apply the 0.005 m minimum after ef_zom(), as a declared CANDIDATA option flagged with EF_H_ZOM_FLOOR_APPLIED.

Missing values propagate. Arguments must be numeric, of length 1 or a common length (length 0 is rejected), and matrix or array arguments must share their dim. Values outside the documented domain, or infinite values, raise an error of class earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error). A missing or unknown method raises earthflux_missing_input or earthflux_unknown_method; an argument required by the chosen method but not supplied to the dispatcher raises earthflux_missing_input. Arguments not used by the method are ignored.

Verification status:

  • "lai": VERIFICADA (SEBAL-Idaho 2002), Waters et al. (2002), p. 27, Eq. 31a, "for agricultural areas" (consistent with their \(z_{om} = 0.12 h\), Eq. 28, and \(h = 0.15\,\mathrm{LAI}\), appendix 2);

  • "ndvi": VERIFICADA (SEBAL-Idaho 2002), Waters et al. (2002), p. 28, Eq. 31b, with coefficients fitted to sample pixels of known roughness (named a and b there);

  • "perrier": VERIFICADA (IAHS 2012), Allen et al. (2012), p. 73 (unnumbered equation; \(f\) = 0.6 is suggested there for mixed forests);

  • "height": VERIFICADA as FAO-56 content; its use in METRIC is not verified (the SEBAL Idaho manual uses 0.12 h for the station surface, Eq. 28, after Brutsaert, 1982).

The cross-check with Allen et al. (2007) remains desirable but is no longer blocking (dev/VERIFICATION.md).

See also

Other aerodynamics and sensible heat functions: ef_air_density(), ef_blending_wind(), ef_calibrate_h(), ef_dt_coef(), ef_h_control(), ef_rah(), ef_sensible_heat(), ef_ts_datum(), ef_ustar()

Examples

# Short crops: z_om = 0.018 * LAI (m)
ef_zom(lai = c(0.5, 2, 4), method = "lai")$zom
#> [1] 0.009 0.036 0.072
ef_zom_lai(c(0.5, 2, 4))
#> [1] 0.009 0.036 0.072

# Exponential NDVI / albedo relation with user coefficients
ef_zom_ndvi(ndvi = 0.6, albedo = 0.2, coef_1 = 0.5, coef_2 = -5)
#> [1] 0.03019738

# Perrier function for an orchard 3 m tall
ef_zom_perrier(lai = 2, f_lai = 0.6, height = 3)
#> [1] 0.6314288

# FAO-56: clipped grass 0.12 m tall around a weather station
ef_zom_height(0.12)
#> [1] 0.01476
